findings.title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this returns 2 instead of 1, and for 100/50 it returns 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, the Next link stays enabled, and clicking it loads an empty page at offset == user_count. It should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (with the existing zero-count special case).

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncates to the first 50 members with no way to reach the rest
findings.body: The members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 and Group#findMembers always sends limit=50, but this same endpoint/model is used by the public discourse/routes/group-members route and templates/group/members.hbs, which have no pagination controls at all (pagination was only added to the admin template). Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups up to 200. Now any group with more than 50 members only ever displays the first 50 alphabetically on its public members page.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset
findings.body: limit and offset are taken from params with only to_i and no clamping. A caller who can view a group can pass limit=1000000 to force counting/serializing the entire membership in one request (automatic groups were previously capped at 200), or a negative limit/offset to trigger a database error and a 500. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Group update silently hides the group when the visible parameter is omitted
findings.body: update guards alias_level with present? and name with an explicit nil check, but assigns group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" unconditionally. Any PUT/PATCH that updates only some fields (for example a rename or alias change from another API client, or the legacy PATCH membership call whose handling was removed) will force visible to false and return success, silently hiding the group. Only assign visible when the parameter is present.

findings.title: Creating a group discards the alias_level chosen in the form
findings.body: The admin form always shows the alias_level combo box and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on create, but the new create action only assigns name and visible. A group created with a non-default alias level is saved with the default 0 while the in-memory Ember object still shows the chosen value, so the setting appears applied until the page is reloaded. Assign params[:alias_level] in create as update does.

findings.title: Stale usernames input leaks between group edit pages
findings.body: AdminGroupController is a singleton and its new plain `usernames` property is never reset; setupController only sets the model and loads members. Text typed into the Add Members selector for one group is still bound and visible when the admin opens a different group, and clicking Add there would submit the previous group's usernames to the new group. Clear controller usernames (and stale paging state) in setupController or after a successful add.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route added in config/routes.rb is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members (and the other remove_member example correctly uses :delete). Controller specs dispatch by action name and bypass routing, so this test would still pass even if the DELETE route were missing or mapped to the wrong action, and it misdocuments the API contract.
